title: Batch complete Discussion overlap refreshes into bounded queries
body:
A complete overlap refresh currently starts a separate gh process and GraphQL request for the first comment page of every Discussion. In a sequential live comparison, retrieving the same 1,207 records took 266 requests / 190.34 seconds before this change and 33 requests / 34.09 seconds afterward. The full record maps were exactly equal, including body, URL and update time; this is one observed run, not a guaranteed timing bound.

Batch ten discussions with the first 25 comments and first 10 replies each (at most 2,760 nested nodes), retaining 100-row continuation requests for every remaining comment/reply page. Record order, all-level coverage, stale-cache reporting and per-source atomic replacement remain unchanged. No new dependency or cache schema is introduced.

Validation: Python 3.12.14 required research tooling suite passes 68 tests with 3 pre-existing Linux-only skips. New independent backing-data fixtures prove 23 small discussions need only 3 requests; busy threads reach later comments and replies without omissions or duplicates; failures on three continuation positions preserve the previous complete cache. Existing pagination fixture updated for the batched initial response. git diff --check passes.

A pre-existing limitation remains: research/overlap-path-index pins find_overlap.py at eb4db436..., while the current-main helper is already e3ab63c8.... That frozen package's registered replay cannot validate the current live helper. Its pins are unchanged; no registered historical replay success is claimed. The current tooling tests and direct live retrieval comparison are separate evidence.

Task selection: bit-mechanisms seed 8e64cea42bbb24185934e9924ff13a6a, changed to a concrete replay-runtime expertise handoff. The initial assembly-inequality lead was retired as overlap with outer-bernstein-certificate. Canonical main 0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2, priority revision 4; final overlap covers 710 open PRs and 1,207 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings. Credit Douglas Colkitt for the overlap helper and Aaron Wang/navinor for the path-index work. New work by ywz65 with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, Apache-2.0. No selected frontier or frozen scientific-source changes.
